titel: 10 Foods That Naturally Boost GLP-1 & Quiet Food Noise

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Ten affordable foods that naturally boost GLP-1 and quiet food noise
kurzfassung: The human body naturally produces the weight-loss hormone GLP-1 through specific foods rather than expensive medications. A recent meta-analysis identifies ten affordable foods—including oats, chia seeds, eggs, and fermented items—that stimulate these hormones and reduce hunger. Incorporating these dietary strategies helps manage appetite naturally while avoiding the pitfalls of pharmaceutical weight-loss treatments.
stichpunkte: L-cells in the intestinal tract respond to specific nutrients by producing the GLP-1 hormone naturally.
Beta-glucan fiber found in oats slows gastric emptying, mimicking the fullness effect of weight-loss drugs.
Protein directly stimulates both GLP-1 and the fullness hormone PYY, making high-protein breakfasts ideal.
Weight-loss drugs often lead to weight regain after stopping, because they do not teach the body to produce its own hormones.
Fiber feeds gut microbes, which in turn produce the hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate appetite.
Apples and cabbage contain fermentable fibers that create short-chain fatty acids to trigger L-cells.
Cooling cooked potatoes turns their starches into resistant starches that stimulate GLP-1 production.
Viscous fibers found in oatmeal show a stronger GLP-1 response in women compared to men.
Black beans and lentils effectively increase the gut fermentation pathway for optimal hormone production.

beschreibung:
If you’re constantly thinking about food, battling afternoon cravings, or struggling to feel satisfied after eating, your fullness hormones may be an important part of the conversation.

In this solo episode, Dr. Mindy breaks down the foods that can support your body’s natural GLP-1 production and explains how fiber, protein, resistant starch, fermented foods, and omega-3-rich foods influence satiety. You’ll learn practical ways to build meals that help you feel fuller longer, support your gut microbiome, and work with your body’s natural appetite signals.
